name: Atomic BEEF (BRC-95): the subject's graph, not the wire position
reference_impl: bsv-rs@0.8.1: the expected values are this crate's ruling (BRC-95's graph followed through the inputs of every raw entry, proven or not; the owner's ruling of 2026-10-22), not the TypeScript SDK's. The bytes are the writers': @bsv/sdk@2.1.4, go-sdk@v1.7.2 and bsv-rs. @bsv/sdk 3.x (ts-stack 4d0ea63, Beef.ts:420-434) cuts the graph at each proven transaction and refuses the two vectors marked intended; it agrees on the other four
description: An atomic BEEF is valid when the subject is a transaction of the BEEF and every other entry is reachable from the subject by following the inputs of raw entries, proven or not (this crate's ruling; @bsv/sdk 3.x stops at each proven transaction, as BRC-95's 'up to the point where each input can be confirmed with a Merkle proof' reads); position is not judged. Each proven entry carries a one-leaf BUMP (a block of one transaction, the root the txid); input.headers is the merkle root per height a chain tracker must carry. Every output is OP_TRUE and every unlocking script empty, so the spends execute. Staged in bsv-rs (tests/transaction/vectors/atomic-beef.json) for vectors/sdk/transactions/.

vectors.description: Dependency order, the subject last: Z (proven), C (unproven, spends Z), W (proven), S2 (spends C and W). As the Go writer writes it (a DFS over the inputs, the subject collected last; the order of the proven entries follows Go's map iteration).
The TypeScript writer's partition order on the same graph: every proven entry first in encounter order (W, Z), then the unproven in dependency order (C), the subject last (S2).

The TypeScript writer's order on Z (proven) -> A (raw, unproven) -> P (proven) -> S1: P is written before its raw unproven ancestor A, which only P spends. BRC-95 judges the graph, not the position: valid. bsv-rs before 0.8.1 refused it UnrelatedTransaction (the bsv-dd x402 refund, P0-65). ts-stack 3.x (@bsv/sdk 3.0.0 at 4d0ea63, npm 3.2.1) refuses it: its closure (Beef.ts:420-434 #collectAtomicTransactions) does not follow the inputs of the proven P, so A is outside it and isAtomic is false (Transaction.fromAtomicBEEF: 'Atomic BEEF contains unrelated transaction data.'). The expected value is bsv-rs's ruling.
vectors.skip_reason: ts-stack 3.x cuts the subject's graph at each proven transaction and refuses a raw ancestor behind a proof; the expected value is bsv-rs's ruling (a stated divergence, bsv-rs CHANGELOG 0.8.1).

vectors.description: The subject present but not last: P, Z, S1, then A (S1's ancestor through the proven P, spending the earlier Z). Every entry is in the subject's graph and every unproven entry follows what it spends: valid. The TypeScript writer never writes this shape (toBinaryAtomic cuts every entry after the subject) nor does the Go writer (the subject last, the ancestry cut at each proof); bsv-rs's writer did, merged in the order P, Z, S1, A, until it emitted the BRC-95 closure (0.8.1, before release; it now drops A, behind the proven P). ts-stack 3.x (@bsv/sdk 3.0.0 at 4d0ea63, npm 3.2.1) refuses it: its closure (Beef.ts:420-434 #collectAtomicTransactions) does not follow the inputs of the proven P, so A is outside it and isAtomic is false (Transaction.fromAtomicBEEF: 'Atomic BEEF contains unrelated transaction data.'). The expected value is bsv-rs's ruling.

vectors.description: An entry outside the subject's graph: X (proven, spent by nothing) beside the S1 graph. BRC-95: nothing else may be present; refused. The TypeScript writer writes it (toBinaryAtomic does not trim an unrelated entry) and its 2.1.4 reader accepts it (Transaction.fromAtomicBEEF, Beef.verifyValid).

The prefix names X, which the BEEF does not hold (the bytes of dependency-order-subject-last with the 32 bytes at offset 4 replaced). Refused. Hand-built: no writer writes an atomic BEEF for a txid it does not hold (TypeScript throws 'does not exist in this Beef', Go 'atomic BEEF subject ... is missing', bsv-rs a BeefError).

Two entries outside the subject's graph, one of them spent: beside the proven subject S, a proven Y and a raw unproven X that spends Y and that nothing spends, written Y, X, S. The walk from S over the inputs of raw entries reaches neither, so the BEEF is refused (BRC-95: nothing else may be present). Y comes before X in the trie order (the txid's bytes, each byte's bits reversed, least first), so bsv-rs's streaming reader (verify_stream, verify_stream_structure; the Lean's finish) names Y (640639c3d0bd8a5ef167e9700ed22e54ac7b79a9872c436cba9f73f1cf5118fe) at offset 124, the earliest unreached entry; the whole-BEEF reader (Beef::verify_structure, verify_valid) refuses it UnrelatedTransaction and names no entry. @bsv/sdk 3.x refuses it (its closure from S stops at the proven S; Transaction.fromAtomicBEEF: 'Atomic BEEF contains unrelated transaction data.' names no entry); @bsv/sdk 2.1.4's readers and go-sdk's NewBeefFromAtomicBytes do not judge the graph. Y's amount is the first from 1,000 up that gives this trie order. Hand-built by bsv-rs's test writer (tests/beef_atomic_graph.rs xy_pair, no sort).

input.writer: bsv-rs tests/beef_atomic_graph.rs xy_pair (hand-built, written as given)
